tool_input.prompt: Research question for the WarMapCodex. Use primary sources only (the person's own posts, mailing-list archives, official project and foundation pages, dated news reports). For each of these seven people: Bradley Kuhn (Software Freedom Conservancy), Michael Downey (GNOME code of conduct), Daniel Fore (elementary OS), Andy Hunt (Agile Manifesto), Howard Chu (OpenLDAP), Richard Felker (musl), Ludovic Courtes (GNU Guix) — give (1) the projects and foundations or boards they are formally involved with, each with a source link and date; and (2) any dated primary-source record of their public stance toward Richard Stallman, including the 2019 resignation and the open letters of 2021, and toward his use of the term "free software". Separately: Codeberg e.V. governance and its code-of-conduct and moderation history, including its February 2025 announcement about "far-right" forces, and the GNU Guix project's May 2025 move of its repositories to Codeberg. Mark every claim as primary source, secondary report, or unverified, and say plainly where no record was found. Do not infer anyone's views from association. A claim circulating online, that several of these people publicly endorsed a post saying "F open source" and redefining free software as an explicitly political bundle, is unverified: look for the original post and for each person's own engagement with it, and report only what you can source.
